extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, examiners, administrative patent judges, and KIPO officials (practitioners in Korean patent prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational rules and standards for interruption, suspension, resumption, submission, and service of patent-related proceedings before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and the Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of request to resume when no grounds exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon examining the request ex officio, that no grounds exist to accept the request for resuming the interrupted proceeding under Article 20, he/she shall determine to dismiss the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner or administrative patent judge may investigate ex officio and dismiss resumption requests found groundless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner/judge determines resumption after certified copy served
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a request for resuming a proceeding interrupted after a certified copy of a decision or a ruling is served, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the administrative patent judge shall determine whether to permit the resumption of the proceeding interrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special procedure applies where resumption request follows service of a certified decision/ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to resume when responsible person fails to resume
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person specified in any subparagraph of Article 21 fails to resume the interrupted proceeding, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the administrative patent judge shall, ex officio, order the person to resume the proceeding within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official may compel resumption by setting a designated period for the named party to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed resumption after designated period expires
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proceeding is not resumed within the period specified, it shall be deemed resumed on the day following the expiration of the period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resumption is not effected within ordered period, law treats the proceeding as resumed automatically the next day; Commissioner/judge must notify all relevant parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of resumption to relevant parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the proceeding is deemed resumed under paragraph (6), the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the presiding administrative patent judge shall notify all relevant parties thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications are required upon deemed or actual resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when Commissioner/judge unable to perform duties
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or an administrative patent judge is unable to perform any of his/her duties due to a natural disaster or other extenuating circumstances, the proceeding pending in the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board shall be suspended until such circumstances cease to exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is automatic in face of KIPO incapacity caused by disasters/extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension when a party faces indefinite-duration impediment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a relevant party is unable to resume a proceeding pending before the Korean Intellectual Property Office or before the Korean Intellectual Property Trial and Appeal Board due to an obstacle that persists for an indefinite duration, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the administrative patent judge may determine to order the suspension of the proceeding until the obstacle is removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Impediments of indefinite duration’ include disrupted communications due to war or long-term illness preventing contact; suspension under this paragraph is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to revoke suspension determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or an administrative patent judge may revoke the determination made under paragraph (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grounds for suspension cease, the official may revoke suspension and resume proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification upon suspension or revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or the presiding administrative patent judge suspends a proceeding under paragraph (1) or (2) or revokes a determination under paragraph (3), he/she shall notify all relevant parties thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All parties must be informed of suspensions and revocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on running of periods when interrupted or suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent-related proceeding is interrupted or suspended, the running of the relevant period shall be interrupted, and the entire period shall start to run again from the time the resumption of the proceeding is notified or the proceeding is resumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time elapsed before interruption/suspension is not counted; the statutory or designated period restarts in full upon resumption. Example: a one-month amendment period that had 15 days elapsed before interruption is reset to one month after resumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: interruption vs suspension of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Discontinuation of a proceeding is divided into interruption (when a cause affecting a party prevents the proceeding until another party appears) and suspension (when a cause affecting KIPO or a party causes legal suspension or suspension by KIPO's decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interruption generally tied to a party-specific legal reason; suspension tied to KIPO incapacity or indefinite impediment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption due to legal reasons and role of legal representative
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent-related proceeding shall be interrupted because of legal reasons regardless of intention of KIPO or a party who initiates the proceeding. However, even in the presence of a cause of interruption, the proceeding shall not be interrupted if there is a legal representative with power of attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence of a valid legal representative with power of attorney prevents interruption despite other causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to resume an interrupted proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties who can resume the interrupted patent-related proceeding include: successor in title or administrator of inherited property (subject to renunciation rules), juristic person after merger, party who recovered capacity or their legal representative, newly-appointed legal representative, newly-appointed trustee when trustee commission terminated, replacement representatives under Article 11(1) proviso, and persons with same qualification when trustee in bankruptcy loses qualification or dies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific categories listed; note renunciation of inheritance rule (successor cannot resume until renounces inheritance is considered). Reference to Civil Act Article 1019 for acceptance/renunciation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting resumption of interrupted proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: An interrupted proceeding can be resumed by submitting a written request stating such intention of resumption; the person shall attach evidential documents of grounds for resumption to the written request and submit them to the Commissioner or presiding administrative patent judge. The Commissioner or President shall notify such request to the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing party may request order to file a request for resumption; requests lacking grounds after ex officio investigation may be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner/judge duty when aware of interruption during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commissioner has become aware of the fact that a ground for interruption of a patent-related proceeding was generated in the middle of an examination, he shall suspend the examination until the point when the proceeding is resumed under Article 21 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners ordinarily proceed without extra investigation into interruption unless they become aware of a ground; upon awareness they must suspend examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when aware of ground for resumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner is aware of a ground for resumption of an interrupted proceeding, he/she shall order a resumption of the proceeding within the designated period in the name of the Commissioner. Where a request for resumption is not filed within the designated period, the request shall be deemed to have been filed; the examiner shall notify such fact to the party and carry out the examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner orders resumption and the party fails to file, the system deems request filed and the examiner proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation and restart when examiner overlooks interruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner overlooks a ground for interruption of a patent-related proceeding and continues an examination procedure, he/she shall invalidate such proceeding and conduct the proceeding from the beginning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an applicant died and examiner issued rejection unaware of death, rejection is illegitimate; examiner must revoke the rejection and reissue a notice for grounds after resumption, providing opportunity to submit written argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic suspension when KIPO unable to carry out duties (natural disaster)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Korean Intellectual Property Office is unable to carry out its duties due to a natural disaster or other extenuating circumstances, the proceeding shall be suspended without any decision of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal decision required for suspension in such circumstances; suspension is automatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to suspend where examination relates to litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examination proceeding of a patent application is related to a trial or litigation and where conducting the examination after the completion of the trial or litigation is deemed appropriate, an examiner can suspend such proceeding by discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may suspend to await outcome of related trial/litigation when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: While interrupted/suspended, KIPO shall not proceed in principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, while a patent-related proceeding is interrupted or suspended, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office or an examiner shall not proceed with the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General prohibition against proceeding while interruption/suspension in effect, subject to statutory exceptions described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor obligation and effect of transfer on continuing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right or any patent-related right is transferred while a proceeding is pending, the Commissioner or presiding administrative patent judge may require the successor in title to continue the proceeding. The effect of the already-initiated proceeding shall reach the successor in title; the proceeding does not need to commence anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall notify intentions to require successor to continue in name of Commissioner. Example: if change of applicant filed within designated period after a notification of grounds for rejection, examiner need not re-send notification to successor and the original period for written argument remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of submitted documents (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application, a request, or any other document submitted to the Commissioner or President under this Act shall take effect from the date when it reaches the Commissioner or the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt = 'when it reaches' the office; different handling rules depend on submission method (mail, electronic, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for documents submitted by post
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitted by post, it shall be deemed received on: 1) the date stamped on the post by a postal authority if clear; 2) if stamp unclear, the date evidenced by the receipt; (special rule: for patent registration or international applications submitted by post, they take effect on the date when received by the Commissioner/President).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where stamped date unclear, evidence of receipt controls; for international applications, effective date is when actually received by KIPO (preferential over ordinary mail rule). Ordinance may prescribe matters for delay/loss/interruption of postal service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing allowed and validity of electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may prepare a patent application and other documents in electronic form according to methods prescribed by Ordinance and submit them via an information and communications network or by electronic recording medium. Electronic documents submitted shall be as valid as paper documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kinds of documents, methods, and other necessary matters for electronic submission are prescribed by Ordinance; electronic submissions are deemed received when submitter can confirm the filing number via the network or when contents recorded in KIPO's system file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting use of electronic documents and digital signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to perform a patent-related proceeding using electronic documents shall report such use to the Commissioner or the President and shall affix his/her digital signature on electronic documents submitted to identify the person who submits the documents. Electronic documents submitted shall be deemed submitted by the person whose digital signature is affixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings for reporting and method of affixing digital signature are prescribed by Ordinance; digital signatures must identify submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification/service via network to reporters of electronic use
rubrics_metrics.description: If KIPO officials intend to give notice of or serve a document to a person who has reported on the use of electronic documents, they may do so via an information and communications network. Such notification/service via network shall be as valid as notification/service in writing and shall be deemed received as the contents recorded in the file of the electronic information processing system used by KIPO when the addressee accesses the document via their system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and kinds/methods of electronic notification/service are prescribed by Ordinance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when domicile unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is impossible to serve a document on a person because his/her domicile or place of business is unknown, service by publication shall be made by publishing the statement that the relevant document is available for delivery in the Patent Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial service by publication takes effect two weeks after date of publication; subsequent service to the same party takes effect the day after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service on overseas residents
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents to be served on an overseas resident shall be served on his/her patent administrator, if appointed. If no patent administrator is appointed, documents may be posted by registered airmail and shall be deemed served on the mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered airmail receipt evidences service date for overseas parties without an appointed agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mail delivery rules to mitigate distance unfairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents are submitted by mail, because distances may differ causing unfairness to distant parties, the time when documents are submitted to a post office is deemed to be the time when the documents reach the Korean Intellectual Property Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule prevents disadvantage to parties living far from KIPO; in practice stamp date or post office submission receipt used to determine effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for international applications and conflicts with PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents regarding an international application submitted by mail shall take effect from the date when they are received by KIPO; if delays/loss occur for international phase mail, Articles 86 or 87 of Enforcement Rules apply, but where PCT Rules (Article 82) provide otherwise, the PCT Rules apply preferentially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International application handling may differ from domestic rules and PCT rules outrank domestic Enforcement Rules where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents that cannot be submitted electronically include: submission of articles (attached electronic documents), a request for correction and issuance, documents related to an international application prepared in Japanese (including Annexed Forms No.35 and 51 with original copies), a request for ruling under Article 214(1), and a request for correction of digitized contents. Applicants filing national defense-related secrecy applications cannot file electronically unless secrecy is cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of excluded documents is specified; submission alternatives and exceptions noted (e.g., can file electronically after secrecy cancelled).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital signing and access credentials for online submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic documents shall be digitally signed using the software operated by KIPO or the KIPO webpage and be submitted. A person who wishes to submit documents online shall enter the applicant code and password to the electronic data processing system using software provided by KIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KIPO-provided software and authentication credentials required for electronic filing; digital signature identifies submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curing missing attachments after online submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person submits documents online and some required documents were not attached, he/she shall attach the missing documents to 'a submission of articles such as attached electronic documents' in Annexed Form No.7 within three days of the day when the applicant confirmed a receipt number and submit the documents in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-day cure period applies after confirmation of receipt number; missing materials must be filed in writing with specific form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous proceedings submission ordering and same-day processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more patent-related proceedings required to be conducted at the same time are submitted online, they shall be entered consecutively. If one is submitted online and the rest by electronic recording medium or in writing, all of the concerned proceedings shall be conducted on the same day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules ensure multiple required simultaneous proceedings are processed together; online/conventional submissions synchronized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service procedures: documents affecting patent rights must be served and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents whose results affect the gain or loss of a patent right or the interest of a party shall be notified and served to a party by a certain procedure. Methods of service include personal service, service by mail and service by publication; details prescribed in enforcement regulations and Presidential Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of documents subject to service include certified copy of decision to grant a patent, notification of invalidation under Article 16(2), certified copy of decision under Article 214(3). For documents affecting rights, government electronic document system (On-nara) may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal service formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal service refers to handing over documents to a party or their representative in person. An examiner shall obtain a receipt stating the date of receipt and the name of the recipient. Alternatively, recipient may write date and name in document service registry and confirm with registered seal. If recipient is not a patent attorney, both the patent attorney’s registered seal and representative’s seal shall be stamped together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipts or registry stamping serve as proof of personal service; special seal stamping rules when recipient not patent attorney (Article 7 of Regulation for Administrative Practices of Dispatch Box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by registered mail practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents shall be conducted by registered mail, except where a party or representative receives documents in person or via an information and communication network. Where documents are served by mail, a receipt of the registered mail issued by a post office shall be placed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered mail receipt evidences mailing and forms part of service record; exceptions exist for personal or electronic service.
